inputs.original_text: KT Rama Rao, the BRS Working President, has accused the Congress government of corruption and deliberately failing to stop illegal mining, naming Raghava Constructions owned by Telangana Information and Public Relations Minister Ponguletti Srinivas Reddy as being involved. This on Sunday, March 29 in Hyderabad makes clear how ruling institutions protect corporate interests tied to those in power. Such inaction is not an oversight but a structural feature that sustains inequality, allowing elites to exploit resources while vulnerable workers and communities face the ongoing consequences of unchecked greed. We need real institutional reform to center labor rights and dismantle these patterns of historical injustice that harm the most marginalized.
inputs.modified_text: KT Rama Rao, the BRS Working President, accused the Congress government of corruption and deliberately failing to stop illegal mining, calling out Raghava Constructions owned by Telangana Information and Public Relations Minister Ponguletti Srinivas Reddy as part of it, during events on Sunday, March 29 in Hyderabad. This is a clear example of how ruling institutions are designed to shield corporate interests connected to those in power, rather than any simple oversight. It's a structural feature that props up inequality, letting elites profit off resource exploitation while vulnerable workers and communities bear the brunt of the damage from this systemic greed. Real institutional reform is essential to prioritize labor rights and dismantle these entrenched patterns of historical injustice that continue harming the most marginalized.
